subject: geography
title: Resources, industry, and development
objective: Compare measures of development and the role of resources.

lesson.opening: Countries differ in wealth and well-being. Geographers measure development in more than one way.

sections.heading: Resources
sections.body: Renewable resources can be replenished, such as sunlight and wind. Non-renewable resources, such as coal and oil, are finite.

sections.heading: Measures
sections.body: GDP per person measures economic output. The Human Development Index adds health and education, giving a fuller picture.

sections.heading: Industry and change
sections.body: Industry often shifts from primary (farming, mining) to secondary (manufacturing) to tertiary (services) as economies develop.

activities.prompt: The Human Development Index includes income, health, and…
Manufacturing belongs to which economic sector?
Explain why GDP alone can mislead about development.
activities.context: Income says nothing directly about health, education, or how evenly wealth is shared.
